title: Find water already in your house
summary: Water heater tank, toilet tank (not bowl), ice, and canned liquid: how to get at it safely.

sources.title: CDC: How to Find Clean Water in an Emergency
Regional Water Providers Consortium: How to access water from your water heater during an emergency
DC Water: How to drain your water heater
FEMA: Where can I find clean drinking water after a disaster?

blocks.text: If the taps stop, there is water in your house already. Use bottled water first. Then use these, and **treat everything before drinking** (boil, bleach or filter).

rows: Water heater tank (the one that feeds your faucets)
Not the separate tank that feeds radiators. Tankless heaters have no tank.
Only if the ice was made from clean water.
Only if the water is clear and has no cleaning chemicals or colored tablets.
Liquid from canned fruit and vegetables
Listed by CDC as a water source.
Never drink from the heating system.

blocks.text: A tank water heater can give you roughly **30 to 80 gallons**.
The water can be **very hot**. Wear gloves and safety glasses. Do not open the drain until the tank has cooled.

blocks.alt: Water heater drain order. 1: turn off the main water supply to the house. 2: cut its power, with the breaker for electric or the pilot setting for gas. 3: close the heater's cold-water supply valve. 4: let air in with the relief valve handle or a hot faucet. 5: put a clean container under the drain valve and open it slowly. Do not open the drain until the tank has cooled.
blocks.caption: The first five water-heater steps below, numbered to match.

items: Find your water heater. Turn off the **main water supply** to the house first, so the tank water stays put.
**Cut its power.** Electric: flip the breaker. Natural gas: turn the control to the **pilot** setting. Don't turn it completely off.
Close the water heater's own cold-water supply valve (turn clockwise until it stops, usually on top).
Let air in: lift the handle on the relief valve on the side of the tank, or open a hot faucet in the house (upstairs is best).
Put a clean container under the **drain valve** at the bottom. Open the valve slowly and fill your containers. Close it to stop. Repeat until you have enough.
Sediment: the first water may be cloudy or sandy. Let it settle and pour it through a coffee filter or clean cloth before you treat it.

blocks.text: DC Water's guide waits **2 hours** after switching the heater off so it can cool. Don't turn the heater back on until it has been refilled and your water service is back.
If the drain valve clogs, call a licensed plumber. Flushing the tank once a year cuts down sediment, so do it before you need the water.

items: Take water from the **tank only**. Never the bowl.
Skip it if the water is colored or the tank has cleaning tablets.
For ice, use ice made from clean tap water. Don't make new ice from questionable water.
Treat all of it: boil for 1 minute or use bleach (see those guides).
